doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Growing up hearing French and Creole; the French-speaking dog and mules
summary: His father spoke Creole and French; the children mostly listened, and he tells of a dog and farm animals that understood only French.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did they speak French or Creole in the family? Oh, he, my father talked real French. He talked both, Creole and French. And probably English much less, huh? That's right.
Did you learn Creole and French as a child before you learned English? Oh, yeah. Well, uh, yeah. When I, when I was a kid, I never talked it much.
And actually, we kids didn't talk it much, but, uh, hardly at all. But that's all we listened to. Uh-huh. We, we, huh? Do you remember it?

Oh, I remember quite a, oh, I remember quite a bit of it. Sure. I can understand most of it now. If you talk real slow, you know. We, we had a, we had a dog that, uh, couldn't even understand English.
No kidding. He would, he would bark with a French accent. What would you say to that? That sounds funny, but it's true.
What would you say to that dog, for example, if you wanted to do something?
Well, uh, uh, uh, it's hard for me to remember now. But, uh, what is this name, the dog's name, uh, uh, uh, what is this dog's name?
It wasn't Joseph, because that's my name. Auguste. No, no, it wasn't Auguste. It's Francois. Yeah, that was his name.

And, uh, well, not on, not only, uh, the dogs, uh, those French people, like, had chickens and hogs and mules and everything. Like, I used to go out in the country to visit my cousins and things. And, uh, I'd follow them along when some of my cousins in a field plowed, and they would talk to this mule in French, or this horse, or whatever it was plowing, and they understood real good.
I would talk to them in English and nothing would happen.
So, would you describe yourself as a real Creole?
